Details

The Details component styles the native <details> and <summary> elements — no JavaScript required. It works with JavaScript disabled and stays fully accessible.

Basic Details

Plain native markup opens with a browser disclosure triangle; the open attribute pre-expands content.

What is the Details component?

It wraps the HTML <details>/<summary> pair with ZAK visual styling. Expansion works without any CSS or JS on our side.

HTML
<details open>
    <summary>What is the Details component?</summary>
    <p>It wraps the native &lt;details&gt;/&lt;summary&gt; pair.</p>
</details>

Styled Details

Use the zak-details class for the full card look with a custom marker that rotates when open.

Styled disclosure
The header row carries a chevron that rotates 90° when the panel opens. Borders, padding and radius follow the design tokens.
HTML
<details class="zak-details">
    <summary>Styled disclosure</summary>
    <div class="zak-details-content">The header row carries a chevron...</div>
</details>

Multiple Open by Default

Compared to accordions, native details allow any number of groups to stay open simultaneously.

Why do we need design tokens?

Tokens keep theming consistent across components and let you re-skin the whole product by overriding a few CSS variables.

Is the library tree-shakeable?

Each component maps to a CSS class and a tiny JS module, so unused pieces can be dropped by your bundler.

Nested Details

Native details nest cleanly and preserve keyboard and screen-reader semantics at every level.

Advanced configuration
Environment variables

ZAK_THEME and ZAK_TOKEN shape runtime behavior; see the setup guide for all keys.

Details vs Collapse vs Expandable Panel

  • Details — native HTML, zero JS, best for content that must work without scripting.
  • Collapse — a raw target animated by JS; ideal when you already have a trigger elsewhere.
  • Expandable Panel — a card pairing data-zak-expandable with a body; component with a header.
  • Accordion — a group of linked items; picks exclusive (single-open) semantics.

CSS Classes & Variables

HTML
/* Class Summary */
details                /* Native element: group state kept in "open" */
summary                /* Native toggle heading */
.zak-details           /* Card-styled details wrapper */
.zak-details-content   /* Body region (only visible when open) */

/* Variables used */
--zak-surface          /* Panel background */
--zak-border           /* Panel border */
--zak-radius-lg        /* Rounded corners */
--zak-text-muted       /* Body text color */

JavaScript

HTML
// No JS needed to expand/collapse native details.

// Enhancement only — read state, or force it:
const el = document.getElementById('styledDetails');
el.open = true;                 // expand
el.open = false;                // collapse

// Listen for user toggles
el.addEventListener('toggle', function () {
    console.log('open?', el.open);
});

Accessibility

  • <summary> is natively focusable and keyboard toggling (Enter/Space) comes free.
  • Screen readers announce the details/summary disclosure semantics automatically.
  • Keep the summary short and meaningful — it names the hidden region.
  • When you need richer styling animations (height transitions) or an accordion group, switch to Collapse / Accordion instead.
